results.title: Sprout Social (SPT) Q2 2026 Earnings Call Transcript | The Motley Fool
results.author: Motley Fool Transcribing
highlights:
- Headcount Reduction -- 20% of the global workforce, announced on July 15 to streamline decision-making and remove organizational layers.
...
Management reported quarterly revenue of $123.8 million and announced a significant workforce reorganization. The company completed a 20% headcount reduction to streamline operations and remove organizational layers, targeting $50 million in annualized cost savings. Strategic focus shifted toward customers contributing more than $30,000 in annual recurring revenue, a cohort that now represents 61.4% of subscription revenue. The company raised its full-year profitability guidance and initiated a $50 million share repurchase program, citing a disconnect between current market valuation and long-term potential.
...
As we announced on July 15th, we made the very difficult but important decision to reduce the size of our team by approximately 20%. We're incredibly grateful for the contributions of our departing colleagues who helped shape Sprout into the company it is today. Our industry and software more broadly is changing quickly, and the way companies need to operate and invest has changed with it. As we step back to examine our own operating model, we saw too many layers and an org structure that was slowing down decision-making, and saw an opportunity to really streamline our work and areas of focus.
...
The buyback reflects our confidence in the durability of our business, our ability to generate free cash flow, and the long-term opportunity we see ahead. We believe it represents a disciplined capital allocation strategy that will allow us to return value to shareholders and offset dilution. Before I discuss guidance, I want to review the recent restructuring and its impact on our financials. We believe the reorganization we announced on July 15th will enable us to deliver faster product innovation for customers in the future, while also enabling us to invest in our business. As part of this headcount reduction, we expect to incur pre-tax restructuring charges of approximately $18 million-$20 million. Substantially all of these changes will impact Q3.
